objects.description: Opaque handle type for the MagickWand API, representing a wand context used to create, read, manipulate, and write images. Only a forward declaration is provided here; the structure is defined privately within the library. Treat as an opaque object managed via the MagickWand API functions.

functions.name: MagickGetException
functions.description: Returns a newly-allocated C string describing the most recent exception for the given MagickWand and stores the exception severity in the provided ExceptionType output parameter. Typical usage is to query after an operation fails, then free the returned message once consumed.
requirements: The MagickWand * argument must be a valid, initialized wand (e.g., created by NewMagickWand, CloneMagickWand, or similar).
The ExceptionType * argument must be a valid, non-null pointer to receive the severity.
The returned char * must be released by the caller (typically using MagickRelinquishMemory) to avoid memory leaks.
Safe to call even if no exception is currently set; content and format of the message in that case are unspecified (inferred).

functions.name: MagickGetExceptionType
functions.description: Returns the severity of the most recent exception associated with the provided MagickWand. Use this to quickly check if an error or warning occurred without retrieving the full message.
requirements: The MagickWand * argument must be a valid, initialized wand.
Return value indicates severity; exact mapping to severities is defined by ExceptionType (details not provided here).

functions.name: IsMagickWand
functions.description: Checks whether the given pointer refers to a valid MagickWand instance. Useful for validation or defensive programming before calling other wand APIs.
requirements: The pointer may be NULL; behavior for NULL is library-defined (commonly returns MagickFalse; exact behavior not specified here).
No side effects on the wand.

functions.name: IsMagickWandInstantiated
functions.description: Indicates whether the MagickWand subsystem has been initialized (i.e., whether MagickWandGenesis has been called).
requirements: Callable at any time to query initialization state.
Return semantics beyond true/false are not documented here; exact initialization conditions are library-defined.

functions.name: MagickClearException
functions.description: Clears the current exception state for the given MagickWand. After this call, subsequent exception queries reflect only later operations.
requirements: The MagickWand * argument must be a valid, initialized wand.
Return value indicates success or failure (MagickBooleanType).
Clears only the exception state; it does not modify images or properties (inferred from name).

functions.name: MagickSetIteratorIndex
functions.description: Sets the current image iterator position of the wand to the specified index within the image list. Enables random access to images in a multi-image wand.
requirements: The MagickWand * argument must be a valid wand containing zero or more images.

The index parameter is a signed size value; valid range is typically 0 to number_of_images-1. Behavior for out-of-range values is library-defined; the function returns MagickFalse on failure (inferred).
If the wand contains no images, the call will fail (inferred).

functions.name: CloneMagickWand
functions.description: Creates a new MagickWand that is a copy of the provided wand, including its image list and state. Use to duplicate a wand for independent modification.
requirements: The source MagickWand * must be a valid, initialized wand.
Returns a new MagickWand * on success or NULL on failure (typical convention; exact failure indicator not documented here).
The returned wand must be destroyed by the caller using DestroyMagickWand to avoid leaks.

functions.name: DestroyMagickWand
functions.description: Destroys a MagickWand, releasing all associated resources and image data. Returns NULL for convenience so callers can assign the result to their wand variable.
requirements: The MagickWand * must be a wand obtained from NewMagickWand, CloneMagickWand, NewMagickWandFromImage, or similar.
After destruction, the pointer must not be used again except to store the returned NULL.
Safe to pass NULL is typical in ImageMagick APIs, but not explicitly documented here; callers should avoid passing invalid pointers.

functions.name: NewMagickWand
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new, empty MagickWand ready for loading or creating images and applying operations.
requirements: Returns a valid wand on success or NULL on allocation failure (inferred).
The returned wand must be destroyed with DestroyMagickWand by the caller.

functions.name: NewMagickWandFromImage
functions.description: Creates a new MagickWand initialized from an existing MagickCore Image object. Useful when bridging from MagickCore APIs to MagickWand.
requirements: The Image * must point to a valid MagickCore Image initialized by MagickCore facilities.

The function likely copies or references image data; ownership semantics are not specified here. Callers should assume the returned wand must be destroyed with DestroyMagickWand, and the original Image remains the caller's responsibility.
Returns NULL on failure (inferred).

functions.name: MagickGetIteratorIndex
functions.description: Returns the current image iterator index within the wand's image list. Use after navigation calls (e.g., MagickSetFirstIterator, MagickSetLastIterator, MagickSetIteratorIndex).
requirements: The MagickWand * must be a valid wand.
Return value is a signed index; exact sentinel for "no current image" is not documented here (commonly -1 in similar APIs; unknown).

functions.name: ClearMagickWand
functions.description: Clears the wand to an empty state, removing images and resetting internal state. Does not destroy the wand itself.
requirements: The MagickWand * must be a valid wand.
After clearing, previous images are discarded; subsequent operations should load or create new images.

functions.name: MagickWandGenesis
functions.description: Initializes the MagickWand API. Typically called once at program start before using other MagickWand functions, especially in environments where implicit initialization is not desired.
requirements: Should be called before other MagickWand operations in applications that require explicit initialization (inferred).

In multi-threaded contexts, ensure initialization occurs in a thread-safe manner; calling multiple times should be harmless or reference-counted in the library, but exact semantics are not specified here (unknown).

functions.name: MagickWandTerminus
functions.description: Shuts down and cleans up the MagickWand API. Typically called once at program termination to release resources allocated by the library.
requirements: Should be called after finishing all MagickWand operations (inferred).
Must not be called while other threads are concurrently using MagickWand (inferred best practice; exact constraints not specified).

functions.name: MagickRelinquishMemory
functions.description: Releases memory allocated by ImageMagick APIs and returns a value suitable for assignment to the freed pointer (commonly NULL). Use this to free strings and buffers returned by MagickWand/MagickCore functions.
requirements: The pointer must either be NULL or a pointer obtained from ImageMagick allocation/return APIs (e.g., MagickGetException).
After the call, the memory must not be accessed.
The return value can be assigned back to the pointer variable to clear it; exact return (typically NULL) is not documented here.

functions.name: MagickResetIterator
functions.description: Resets the wand's image iterator to its initial state for iteration over the image list. Use before iterating images sequentially.
requirements: The MagickWand * must be a valid wand.
If the wand has no images, subsequent iteration may yield no elements; exact iterator semantics are not documented here.

functions.name: MagickSetFirstIterator
functions.description: Sets the current image in the wand to the first image in the list, preparing for forward iteration.
requirements: The MagickWand * must be a valid wand.
The wand should contain at least one image; if empty, behavior is unspecified (likely no current image).

functions.name: MagickSetLastIterator
functions.description: Sets the current image in the wand to the last image in the list, preparing for reverse or position-based operations.
requirements: The MagickWand * must be a valid wand.
The wand should contain at least one image; if empty, behavior is unspecified (likely no current image).
